title: Katharine Hepburn's birth chart
metaDescription: Katharine Hepburn's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 20.8° Taurus. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Cardinal signs carry five of the nine placements whose signs are settled — the broadest certain weighting in the chart. Cardinal weight is read as initiative: the instinct to be the reason something began.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 20.8° Taurus, inside the third decan (20°–30°), whose traditional sub-ruler is Saturn. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Mercury holds 7.6° Taurus, Venus holds 18.1° Aries, Mars holds 15.7° Capricorn — in the old shorthand, thought with its feet on the ground; attraction declared rather than implied; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury to Jupiter is the closest call of the day, a sextile within 1.3°. The scheme reads a sextile as a door left unlocked. Useful, and entirely dependent on someone walking through it. Behind it, Jupiter conjunction Neptune at 1.6°, and Uranus opposition Neptune at 1.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: No closed figure — no grand trine, t-square, or grand cross — holds among the day-stable angles. The chart distributes its tension pair by pair rather than through one standing structure.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, three placements stand out. Venus in Aries at 18.1° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Mars in Capricorn at 15.7° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Jupiter in Cancer at 9.0° is in exaltation. Dignity is a statement about conditions, not about worth.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Tallied where the signs are certain — 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day — the chart gives earth 4, water 3, fire 1, air 1, and cardinal 5, fixed 2, mutable 2 across the modes. An earth emphasis reads as patience with material reality — slow hands, durable results. Uranus was retrograde — apparent backward motion from where the Earth sits, which the tradition reads as a function turned inward before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Taurus into Gemini during that day at the birthplace, travelling 12.2° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
